what: Is vLLM's PLE disk offload (PR #59958, merged 2026-10-30: the n-gram PLE table is read row by row from the safetensors files instead of held in memory) numerically identical to holding the table in pinned CPU memory? Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 (local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4, 99 GiB checkpoint), vLLM 0.33.0rc1.dev451+g5d55ef159 (nightly), one rented RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (Sweden, driver 615.71.09), eager, --language-model-only, max-model-len 4096, max-num-batched-tokens 2048, --disable-flashinfer-autotune (so both runs use the same kernels), thinking off. 48 prompts, max 200 tokens, greedy, sequential and 16 concurrent (vllm_determinism.py), once with --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": true}' and once with '{"disk_offload": true}'.
batch_invariant: refused: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 fails with 'batch_invariant mode is not supported for GDN_ATTN' (the model's gated-delta-net linear-attention layers), so this hybrid model has no exact cross-batch tier in vLLM today
cpu_offload_vs_disk_offload_sequential: 0 of 7,806 positions differ (top-20 logprobs to 1e-4): disk offload is bit-identical to the in-memory table
cpu_offload_vs_disk_offload_concurrent16: 32 of 48 replies diverge, but concurrency changes replies within each mode too (cpu: 42 of 48 diverge sequential vs concurrent; disk: 41 of 48), as expected without batch invariance
memory: weights on the GPU 70.1 GiB in both modes (the table is never on the GPU with either option); disk offload loaded in 37 s vs 56 s
setup_notes: vLLM nightly from wheels.vllm.ai needed: the prebuilt flashinfer-jit-cache wheels (flashinfer.ai/whl/cu130) because pip's nvcc 13.4 mismatches the CUDA 13.0 runtime headers; --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 and gpu-memory-utilization 0.86 (FlashInfer autotune dummy runs at the default batch went out of memory on 96 GB); --disable-flashinfer-autotune, since autotuning picks kernels by timing at startup and could make two otherwise identical servers compute differently.
verdict: Reading model weights from disk instead of memory changes where the numbers come from, not the numbers: a referee need not care whether a provider uses it. The PLE lookup is a gather, so this is what one expects; it is now measured. What does matter for verification here is the model family: hybrid linear-attention models are not batch-invariant in vLLM, so they get the statistical tier (or an exact tier only for providers that serve one request at a time).
